topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission

audits.title: An audit cycle of physical health monitoring and record keeping of long term in-patients at male and female psychiatric rehabilitation wards using QI approach
audits.standard: NICE guidelines, RCPsych report on physical health in mental health and Cygnet Health Care physical health policy
audits.setting: Male and female long-term psychiatric rehabilitation wards (Cygnet Health Care)

cycle1.result: Physical assessment within 24 hours 98%; monthly physical health reviews 62%; annual Health Improvement Profile 30%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 10%; ECG/bloods for antipsychotic monitoring 64%.

audits.intervention: QI approach with 4 PDSA cycles: MDT strategies to improve engagement with monthly physical health clinics, care plan points, diary reminders for bloods and ECGs, MDT and patient health education, and a designated support staff member for observations and physical health files.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 92%; high-dose antipsychotic monitoring 100%; monthly physical health clinics 88%; annual HIP 75%; annual antipsychotic monitoring/bloods/ECG 95%.

audits.other_findings: At baseline 10 female and 12 male patients regularly refused observations, weights and physical health monitoring.
audits.citation: Tahseen H, Bramall P. An audit cycle of physical health monitoring and record keeping of long term in-patients at male and female psychiatric rehabilitation wards using QI approach. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S107-S108. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.318.

audits.title: An audit of ECG monitoring in patients admitted to the general adult wards at clock view hospital
audits.standard: Mersey Care physical health policy: ECG within 24 hours of admission; NICE and RCP guidance
audits.setting: General adult inpatient wards, Clock View Hospital, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 31/60 had an ECG within 24 hours; of the other 29, reason documented in 16. 13 abnormal ECGs, only 3 referred for further investigation.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: No documentation of the ECG report in one third of cases. Recommended induction teaching and training ward nurses to perform ECGs.

audits.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

audits.title: Implementation of physical examination pro forma – a complete audit cycle
audits.standard: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission
audits.setting: Inner city hospital psychiatric ward

cycle1.result: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23% compliance); 6 had examination in ED before admission.

audits.intervention: Results presented to MDT and NCHDs; colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and briefed to all staff

cycle2.result: 7 examined on admission, 2 refusals documented; 100% compliance (examination done or reason documented).

audits.other_findings: Proforma to be audited every 6 months.

audits.title: Audit of the use of the physical health improvement (PHIT) to document physical health examination on an electronic health record at a mental health trust in Manchester
audits.standard: Local priority: initial physical examination, admission bloods and ECG completed and documented on the PHIT tool in PARIS
audits.setting: Park House inpatient unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 73% had an initial physical examination, 84% admission bloods and 74% admission ECG; recording on the PHIT tool was 33-42%. Valid refusal reason documented in 63-91% of refusals.

audits.title: Audit of physical health monitoring on admission to Mill Lodge (CAMHS Inpatient Unit, York)
audits.standard: Tier 4 CAMHS service specification 2.6.3: assessment, care plan and physical examination within 24 hours of admission (100%)
audits.setting: Mill Lodge Tier 4 CAMHS inpatient unit, York

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours (excluding refusals): physical examination 85%, bloods 82%, ECG 84%; during admission bloods and ECG 100%, examination 90%.

audits.intervention: Planned support for ward staff and on-call junior doctors; re-audit in twelve months.
audits.other_findings: No reason documented for several missed procedures (3 examinations, 2 bloods, 3 ECGs); one blood test delayed by lack of blood tubes.

audits.title: Adherence to the Admission Policy in a Local Old Age Psychiatric Unit in Wrexham: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Local Health Board acute inpatient admission policy: clerking and physical examination within 12 hours, bloods and medication chart within 2 hours, ECG at admission
audits.setting: Old age psychiatric inpatient unit, Wrexham, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: Clerking within 12 hours 67%; physical examination 52%; bloods within 2 hours 24%; ECG at admission 14%; medication chart within 2 hours 90%.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: Barriers included patient agitation, poor inter-team communication, no online handover system and junior doctor workload; recommendations included handover, training nurses and HCAs in phlebotomy and ECG, and ward-based doctor cover.

audits.setting: Norbury House PICU, St George's Hospital, Stafford, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: TFTs 71%; glucose 6%; prolactin 77%; calcium 94%; unnecessary tests in 88% of patients (23 tests).

audits.title: Audit and Quality Improvement of Physical Health of New Admissions to an Acute Inpatient Facility
audits.standard: NSFT Physical Healthcare Policy (C84): baseline bloods, physical examination and ECG within 24 hours of admission; 100% compliance
audits.setting: Samphire ward, acute inpatient unit, Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Physical examination or documented refusal 34.5%; ECG or refusal 53%; bloods or refusal 68%, correct bloods 4.5%; all three components 0%.

audits.intervention: A3 visual aid placed on the ward.

cycle2.result: Physical examination 47%; ECG 61%; bloods 71%, correct bloods 33%; all three components 33%.

audits.other_findings: Ward doctors adhered to the standard significantly more than duty doctors. Induction teaching and a wider re-audit (VTE, height/weight, nursing elements) recommended.

audits.title: Completing the Cycle: Re-Audit of Rotherham Specific Inpatient Physical Health Management and Documentation Following a 2021 Trust-Wide Audit
audits.standard: Trust standards: initial medical examination within 24 hours of admission, documented capacity to consent, chaperone for examinations beyond appearance, pulse or blood pressure, and chaperone gender preference offered
audits.setting: Rotherham psychiatric inpatient wards (acute adult, rehabilitation, PICU, older adult), RDaSH NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Good results for examination within 24 hours and capacity consideration; inadequate results for chaperone presence and chaperone gender preference (no figures given).

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the 2021 Trust-wide audit (not described).

cycle2.result: Nearly 90% examined by a doctor within 24 hours; chaperone documented in only 14%; no patient offered choice of chaperone gender; capacity documented in one third.

audits.other_findings: Older adult wards performed better. Planned next step is teaching at junior doctor induction and a further re-audit.
audits.citation: Bell L, Jenkinson J, Allan L. Completing the Cycle: Re-Audit of Rotherham Specific Inpatient Physical Health Management and Documentation Following a 2021 Trust-Wide Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S150-S150. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.404.

audits.title: A Re-Audit of ECG Monitoring in Patients Admitted to the General Adult Inpatient Wards at Clock View Hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: ECG within 24 hours of admission, documented ECG report, and further investigation of abnormal ECGs
audits.setting: Three general adult inpatient wards, Clock View Hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 52% had ECG within 24 hours; no documented ECG report in 35%; 23% of abnormal ECGs further investigated.

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the original audit (not described).

cycle2.result: 57 (62%) had ECG within 24 hours; 16 (17%) after 24 hours; 19 (21%) never; no documented report in 13%; abnormal ECGs further investigated in 9/16 (56%).

audits.other_findings: Reason for not doing an ECG was documented for 32 (91%). Recommended an electronic alert if no ECG within 24 hours and copying reports to the ward clerk or consultant PA.
audits.citation: Elagamy Y, John C, Dacosta A, Hyland D, Hassan N, Nankoo R. A Re-Audit of ECG Monitoring in Patients Admitted to the General Adult Inpatient Wards at Clock View Hospital, Liverpool, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S155-S155. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.416.

audits.title: Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients
audits.standard: RCPsych Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: bloods within 24 hours of admission; standardised PICU blood panel
audits.setting: Psychiatric intensive care unit, KMPT trust

cycle1.result: 30% bloods within 24 hours, 10% on previous ward, 40% declined/unsafe, 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant tests, 23% some.

audits.intervention: Standardised PICU guideline with pre-filled blood test request form

cycle2.result: Only 6% not done within 24 hours; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised tests; conclusion reports 77% to 100% for full tests and 80% to 94% within 24 hours.

audits.other_findings: Completion remained lower for patients transferred from other wards. Plan to roll out pre-filled forms across all trust wards.
audits.citation: Lawson J, Zabrzycki D, Satisha S. Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S166-S167. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.441.

audits.title: An Audit Reviewing the Completion and Quality of the Admission, Then Six Monthly ALL-Physical Health Assessments (A Six Monthly Health Check) on a Low Secure, Inpatient Forensic Psychiatric Ward in Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Local Trust guidance: mandatory ALL-Physical Health Assessment on admission and six-monthly thereafter (14 categories)
audits.setting: Pine Ward, 17-bed male low-secure inpatient forensic psychiatric ward, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 76.4% of patients had an ALL done; 67.2% of completions green, 15.5% amber, 17.2% red. QRISK 70%, alcohol 58%, diet 82%, exercise 70%, diabetic status 58%, smoking 76% documented.

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: 15/17 (88%) had an ALL in the last 6 months; 89.9% of completions green, 4.6% amber, 5.5% red. QRISK, alcohol, diet and exercise 100% documented; diabetic status 82%, smoking 88%.

audits.other_findings: Some ALL categories were still not completed to the expected standard; authors recommend raising the importance of the assessment with trainees.

audits.title: Improving Physical Health Monitoring on a Working-Age General Adult Inpatient Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Completion and timeliness of physical health checks (examination, observations, height/weight, ECG, bloods, cardiometabolic checklist)
audits.setting: Working-age general adult acute psychiatric inpatient ward

cycle1.result: Physical examinations completed in 93%.

audits.intervention: Daily MDT reviews, job list integration and master list; then a whiteboard with colour coding for task tracking, post-MDT reviews, staff reminders and induction sessions.

cycle2.result: Physical examinations 100%; physical observations maintained at 100%; reduced delays and more BMI measurements completed.

audits.other_findings: Barriers included gender-based refusal of ECGs and reluctance of patients with eating disorders to have BMI measured.
audits.citation: Muhammed M, Jawed A, Yoganathan N. Improving Physical Health Monitoring on a Working-Age General Adult Inpatient Ward: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S152-S152. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.

audits.title: Improving Admission Clerking and Physical Health Checks in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients. A Quality Improvement Project (QIP)
audits.standard: Local and NHS trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission
audits.setting: Battersea Bridge House Hospital, 22-bed acute mental health facility (three wards)

cycle1.result: All five criteria completed within 72 hours in 27 patients (62.8%); delayed in 14 (33.6%); 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests.

audits.intervention: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with emphasis on patient rapport.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention; reported 1.76-fold increase in timely protocol completion, 1.39-fold reduction in delays and 4-fold drop in patient refusal.

audits.other_findings: Delays were mainly due to patient agitation, refusal of bloods or ECG, delayed consent and slow laboratory results; reasons were not documented for 2 patients.
audits.citation: Mubashir R, Arooj B. Improving Admission Clerking and Physical Health Checks in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients. A Quality Improvement Project (QIP). BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S137-S137. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11255.

audits.title: Audit of Admission Blood Tests and Vitamin D Pathway Adherence Amongst New Admissions to an Inpatient Psychiatry Unit
audits.standard: RCPsych guidance: admission blood tests within 24 hours of admission; Trust policy on vitamin D and calcium assessment and management of deficiency
audits.setting: Inpatient adult working age psychiatry unit (excluding PICU), South West Yorkshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 79% had bloods within 24 hours; 75% of delays had a reason documented. FBC, U&E and LFTs done in 84%, TFTs and haematinics 79%, lipids and calcium 74%, HbA1c and prolactin 63%, glucose 53%. Vitamin D checked in 68%; all with significant deficiency had loading doses but only 50% with mild deficiency were prescribed vitamin D. Of discharged patients with significant deficiency, 75% had ongoing supplementation and none had a calcium re-check plan on the discharge letter.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: Vitamin D status: 23% sufficient, 31% mild deficiency, 54% significant deficiency. Follow-up after loading dose therapy was poor.
audits.citation: Brown L, Ngwenya K. Audit of Admission Blood Tests and Vitamin D Pathway Adherence Amongst New Admissions to an Inpatient Psychiatry Unit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S283-S284. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11741.
